Adversarial re-review of J1's own diff found a real latent bug it survived past your own fixture-contamination fix: tests/components/readme/composition/test_authoring.py::test_undocumented_type_count_grows_sub_linearly_not_proportionally still splices *FACTS.facts (the shared module fixture) into its synthetic document, unlike the other 5 new tests. It currently xfails correctly only because FACTS's existing public_symbol facts happen to lack a symbol_kind attribute, excluding them from undocumented_types()'s filter by accident, not design. Verified concretely: adding one plausible future class-kind fact to the shared FACTS fixture flips this to an unexpected XPASS under strict=True, breaking CI for a reason unrelated to real boundedness. Fix: rebuild this one test's document as fully synthetic, matching the pattern your own commit message already claims all 6 tests use. Small, isolated, no other J1 changes need touching.

URGENT, red hosted CI on main right now (run 34483249349, all 3 Python versions, d2bf283): tests/components/readme/extractors/platforms/test_cpp_examples.py::test_an_undeclared_binding_is_not_verified_but_a_real_type_error_still_fails FAILS on the hosted Ubuntu runner's GCC (local run was green - environment divergence, not flaky, identical failure on 3.11/3.12/3.13). Test compiles 'sheet.Save("out.bin"); auto value = Missing::Create();' expecting NOT_VERIFIED, gets FAILED instead - unbound_identifiers()'s all-diagnostics-must-match requirement is likely failing because hosted GCC's version/output includes a diagnostic line neither of your two regexes match (possibly a cascading error from the unresolved sheet.Save call, or a differently-worded scope-qualified shape). Per loop-prompt.md's own rule: hosted CI red is next iteration's first work, before row 9. Reproduce with the real hosted GCC version if possible (or get its exact stderr via gh api repos/babar-raza/repository-presenter/actions/jobs/<id>/logs for a fresh run once you push a fix attempt), widen the pattern to the real diagnostic text, don't guess. This is the same lesson H/G already taught one layer further in: pilot-proof crossed candidates but not toolchain/environment.

STOP guessing - this is now 2 failed attempts on the same hosted-CI-red test (d2bf283, fcfcf6e), same assertion, same result even after removing the auto-deduction construct. Per loop-prompt.md's own rule: two equivalent failed attempts prohibit a third equivalent attempt - change the evidence, not the guess. Confirmed via job logs: no raw GCC diagnostic text is captured anywhere in the CI output (the test only asserts receipt.outcome), and the workflow has no explicit g++/gcc install step to pin a version and inspect it offline. cpp_examples.py's ExampleReceipt already has a stderr field (line ~155/423, clipped compiler output) - change the failing assertion to include it as a message, e.g. `assert [...] == [...], receipts[0].stderr` (or receipts[1].stderr, whichever), push that as its own small diagnostic-only commit, read the real hosted GCC output from the resulting CI log (even if red), THEN fix unbound_identifiers() against the real text - not another guess. This IS real evidence-gathering, not scope creep.

ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (not a guess) from f665d3d's own diagnostic output: hosted GCC emits Unicode curly quotes - literal text is e2 80 98 (U+2018 LEFT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK) sheet e2 80 99 (U+2019 RIGHT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK) was not declared in this scope - but _UNBOUND_IDENTIFIER (cpp_examples.py:56-58) is r"'([^']+)' (?:was not declared in this scope|has not been declared)" - plain ASCII apostrophes only, can never match curly quotes. This is a well-known GCC behavior: diagnostic quote style depends on locale/version (UTF-8 locales default to fancy quotes). Local Windows/MinGW apparently emits plain quotes, hosted Ubuntu GCC emits curly ones - pure environment divergence, nothing to do with auto-deduction or the test's own construct at all (both prior guesses were addressing a non-issue). Fix: widen the regex's quote character class to accept both ASCII ' and Unicode single-quote‘/’ (U+2018/U+2019) on both sides, e.g. r"['‘]([^'’]+)['’] (?:was not declared in this scope|has not been declared)" or equivalent. Also check rust_examples.py's unbound_values() (this file's own comment says it's the same check for rustc's E0425) for the identical latent bug - not confirmed broken, but same risk class, worth a quick look while in this area. Revert the diagnostic-only assertion-message change once fixed and reverified, or keep it (harmless either way, your call). This closes the taskcard for real this time.
